system:
You draft public warning messages for a national alerting authority.
You receive event inputs (each marked verified or unverified) and the issuing context.
Write one alert in English as CAP 1.2 fields.

- Use only facts present in the verified inputs. Do not add places, numbers, times or hazards that are not there.
- Leave unverified inputs out of the alert, and say why in `left_out`.
- `description` is the text shown on the phone by cell broadcast: plain words, under 280 characters, hazard + where + until when, if known.
- `instruction` is the protective action in one or two short sentences.
- Pick CAP values honestly: status from the context (Actual for a real event, Exercise for a drill), severity and urgency from the inputs.
- `note_for_reviewer` is one or two sentences for the human approver: what you were unsure about.
user:
Issuer: Demo national authority (stands in for the real issuer)
Context: real event
Target area (chosen by the operator): Eastern, southern and western areas (demo zone)

Event inputs:
1. [verified; NCM via WAM, 2026-08-22, https://www.wam.ae/en/article/c1v24bo-ncm-forecasts-light-heavy-rain-across-several-uae] ABU DHABI, 22nd August, 2026 (WAM) -- The National Centre of Meteorology (NCM) issued an alert over the possibility of convective cloud formation accompanied by light to moderate rainfall, which may become heavy at times. The alert is in effect from 13:30 on Saturday until 21:00 the same day. The NCM said the weather conditions are expected to affect some eastern, southern and western areas, extending to parts of the country's interior.
2. [verified; issuer profile] Issuer public site (demo): https://alerts.example.ae
3. [verified; institution reviewers] Objections from the institution reviewers to your previous draft. Fix what is within the verified inputs; do not add facts: Network operator and regulator reviewer objects (phone_text.en): The English text is 217 GSM-7 characters and needs 3 cell broadcast pages, against the UAE advice of 1 page. A GSM-7 page holds 93 characters, so readers on many handsets will see only fragments or have to page through. Fix: Cut the English text to 93 GSM-7 characters or fewer, with the hazard and action first. Example: 'NCM: Heavy rain possible E, S, W & interior UAE Sat 22 Aug 13:30-21:00. Avoid valleys & floods.' Drop the 'convective clouds with light to moderate rain' detail. [cites 3GPP TS 23.038 Alphabets and language-specific information, version 18.0.0 Release 18 (ETSI TS 123 038 V18.0.0), p.15] | Network operator and regulator reviewer objects (phone_text.ar): The Arabic text is 215 UCS-2 characters and needs 6 cell broadcast pages, against the 1-page limit. A UCS-2 page is 82 octets, which is about 41 characters, so the Arabic version is badly over length. Fix: Rewrite the Arabic as a minimal one-page message, about 41 UCS-2 characters, giving the hazard and the action, for example heavy rain plus avoiding valleys. Move the timing and area detail to a follow-up message or link. If one page cannot carry the required hazard and action in Arabic, refer the page-limit trade-off to the operators or TDRA for a decision. [cites 3GPP TS 23.038 Alphabets and language-specific information, version 18.0.0 Release 18 (ETSI TS 123 038 V18.0.0), p.15] | Network operator and regulator reviewer objects (phone_text): Neither language contains a protective action. The text only describes possible rain and the validity period, so the first page cannot carry an instruction to the public. Fix: Add a short protective action in both languages and put it on the first page, for example 'Avoid valleys and flooded roads' or 'تجنب الأودية والطرق المغمورة'. [cites Wireless Emergency Alerts; Amendments to Part 11, Report and Order (DA 25-12), multilingual WEA templates, p.21]

left_out: No unverified inputs were received, so nothing was left out for that reason.

Left out the date '22 Aug' from the phone text to stay within one page. 'Sat' and the 13:30-21:00 window are kept.
Did not write Arabic text, because this task covers the English CAP fields only.
data.note_for_reviewer: The phone text is 90 GSM-7 characters. It turns NCM's 'light to moderate, may become heavy at times' into 'heavy rain possible', and the action 'avoid valleys and flooded roads' comes from the reviewer, not from NCM. Please confirm both are acceptable. The one-page (about 41-character) Arabic version still needs to be written; if it cannot carry both hazard and action, refer it to the operators/TDRA.
